maya: Heads up — ran into a weird mypy/pyright mismatch with the new autogen models + async streaming responses. Repro below and wondering if we should patch the generator or just document a workaround.

maya: Short summary: when the SDK returns a streaming ChatResponse (async iterator that yields chunks typed as Union[MessageDelta, ErrorDelta]), pyright accepts it but mypy complains because the autogenerated Pydantic models use a bare Union without a discriminator.

maya: Minimal repro (python 3.11, mypy 1.6):
```py
from redwood import AsyncChatClient
async for chunk in client.stream_chat(resp_id):
    # mypy: error: "Iterator[Any]" has no attribute "type" (simplified)
    if chunk.type == "message":
        pass
```

jonathan: ugh. do you have the exact mypy error? seems like mypy is losing the precise union type on the async iterator return.

maya: error was something like: "error: Item of \"AsyncIterator[object]\" has incompatible type \"object\"; expected \"Union[MessageDelta, ErrorDelta]\"" — looks like the generator signature becomes AsyncIterator[Any] after codegen.

liam: is the generator annotated as -> AsyncIterator[Union[MessageDelta, ErrorDelta]] in the stub? if not that's probably the generator template bug.

maya: yep, in the generated models file the streaming function is annotated but inside the package build step it gets rewritten to -> AsyncIterator[object] (I suspect because of from __future__ imports + our codegen path).

sara: can you paste the generated signature? also which pydantic version? v2 has some typing differences.

maya: generated signature in api_client.py:
```py
async def stream_chat(self, id: str) -> AsyncIterator[object]:
    ...
```

maya: pydantic==2.4.1. The model classes MessageDelta/ErrorDelta are BaseModel subclasses.

liam: ok that's the bug — generator template uses a placeholder and a post-process pass that should replace object with the union but misses streams. i'll dig. we can hotfix by editing the template to inline the union when return_type.kind == 'stream'.

jonathan: workaround in user code: cast the iterator elements when you iterate: `for chunk in cast(AsyncIterator[Union[MessageDelta, ErrorDelta]], client.stream_chat(id)):` still ugly though.

maya: confirmed that cast fixes mypy locally. pyright didn't care. We should also update sample-apps to show the cast until generator is patched.

sara: another idea: change generated chunk classes to include a discriminant field (kind: Literal["message","error"]) so users can narrow with isinstance checks or `if chunk.kind == "message":` Which is also good for runtime safety.

liam: agreed. Adding a discriminator improves runtime and downstream type narrowing. patch incoming. I'll open a PR referencing this thread.

liam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 (WIP) — adds union discriminator and fixes codegen for stream return types.

ci-bot: build/flake8 triggered for PR #842 — CI queued.

jonathan: once PR merges, we should add a tiny unit test in devex-samples that runs mypy on the sample-app to prevent regressions.

maya: yup — I'll add a sample under examples/streaming_typing_check.py showing `async for chunk in client.stream_chat(...)` and a mypy run in the CI job.

sara: Thanks for the clear repro and the temporary workaround. can we also add a blurb in the changelog under "python sdk" so customers searching for typing issues find it?

liam: will do. tagging this thread with `bug:py-sdk-typing` on the PR.

maya: sweet. closing my local issue after trying the cast workaround. will follow up if CI still complains. :thumbsup:

jonathan: nice work everyone, very low-friction fix.

maya: one more note — for customers using pyright-only flows we might still be okay, but our docs should recommend running mypy on critical code paths.

liam: agreed. created an issue in our docs repo to add a short paragraph about typing checks for generated SDKs. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/213

maya: awesome — thanks all.
